events.title: American Society of Botanical Artists 29th Annual International Exhibition
events.description:
[vc_row][vc_column][vc_single_image image=”159826″ add_caption=”yes” css=””][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_column_text css=””]The American Society of Botanical Artists (ASBA) and the Society of Illustrators present the 29th Annual International, ASBA’s second biennial appearance in the historic five-story townhouse on East 63rd Street in New York. The exhibition of 50 original botanical artworks will be installed in the third floor Garden Gallery.

The selection jury of Steve Compton, Patricia Jonas, Arabelle Liepold, and Jeanne Reiner met in May, selecting 50 artworks from 205 entries, including 11 first-time artists. events.title: RIBBIT: The Art of the Amphibian & Reptile
events.description:
[vc_row][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_empty_space height=”26px”]

Opening Reception
October 22 • 5:00pm – 9:00 PM

[vc_empty_space height=”20px”][vc_separator color=”custom” accent_color=”#dd3333″][vc_empty_space][vc_column_text css=””]From whimsical storybook frogs to scientifically observed species, RIBBIT celebrates the fascinating world of amphibians & reptiles and their enduring place in art, folklore, literature, and visual storytelling.

For centuries, amphibians have leapt through myths, fairy tales, and illustration, symbolizing transformation, mystery, resilience, and renewal. Their remarkable journey between water and land has made them powerful visual metaphors, while their unusual forms, colors, and expressive personalities continue to captivate both artists and their audiences.

From children’s books and comics to fantasy, environmental narratives, and scientific illustration, amphibians and reptiles offer endless possibilities for interpretation.
